subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: When the origin is shifted to (−1,2) by the translation of axes, find the transformed equation of x²+y²+2x−4y+1=0.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.57 — SAQ chapter 8 Transformation of Axes, answer 49.1, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what x and y become under the shift, and say which letters the answer must be written in.

steps.label: Take the given equation
steps.margin_note: First mark. The equation you are handed is the ORIGINAL one, so it is the one written in small x and small y. Number it (1) — the last step refers back to it.
steps.memory_tip: This one is the ORIGINAL, in small x and y. Number it (1) — the last step refers back.

steps.why: The first move is to label which equation you were handed. A transformation question is always one of two shapes — given the original find the new, or given the new find the original — and every later step depends on which.
common_mistakes: Treating the given equation as the NEW equation and solving the wrong way round.
Losing the equals-zero when copying the equation down.

steps.label: Write the change of axes
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A shift of origin to (−1, 2) means x = X + h and y = Y + k. Substituting the numbers gives the two lines to carry forward.
steps.memory_tip: A FORWARD shift means x = X + h and y = Y + k. With h = −1 that gives x = X − 1.
lines: We take new origin (h, k) = (−1, 2), then

recall.must_convey: That the new origin is (−1, 2) and the change of axes is x = X + h, y = Y + k.
accept: x equals capital X plus h and y equals capital Y plus k
the new origin is h comma k so substitute x equals X plus h
write the translation formulas with the given shift
new origin teesukoni x equals X plus h ani rayali
shift of origin means x is X plus h and y is Y plus k

steps.why: A shift of origin to (h, k) means an old coordinate is the new coordinate plus the shift: x = X + h and y = Y + k. Nothing rotates, so x depends only on X and y only on Y.
common_mistakes: Writing x = X − h instead of x = X + h.
Swapping h and k when the shift has a negative coordinate.

steps.label: Substitute into the equation
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Put those two lines into equation (1). Every x and every y goes, including the ones inside brackets and squares.
steps.memory_tip: Every x and y goes, including the ones inside brackets and squares.

recall.must_convey: That the two change-of-axes lines are put into the given equation.

steps.why: Substitution is mechanical once the formulas are down. Every x and every y in the given equation is replaced, including the ones inside a squared bracket.
common_mistakes: Substituting into only some of the terms.
Forgetting to substitute inside a squared bracket.

steps.label: Simplify to the answer
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Expand, collect and read off the transformed equation in capital X and capital Y. The answer must be written in the NEW letters, never mixed with the old ones.
steps.memory_tip: The linear terms cancel completely here — the shift was to the circle's own centre.

recall.must_convey: That expanding and collecting gives X² + Y² − 4 = 0.

steps.why: The answer is an equation in the NEW axes, so it must contain only X and Y. A stray x or y means a term was missed in the substitution.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer in small x and y.
Sign slip when expanding a squared bracket.
